title: Programs
meta_description: Music is already a mental health tool. Sounds of Saving helps young people use it intentionally, through artist storytelling, a high-school program, and mental-health resources at concerts, festivals, and campuses.
heading: Programs
lead: Music is already a mental health tool. We help young people use it intentionally. Everything we do starts with something young people are already doing every day: listening. Artists tell the truth about a hard time and the song that got them through it. Schools get a five-session program built on the music students already love. And we show up where music and community already exist, with real resources and a way to get help.

steps.label: Artists
steps.body: Films and stories where artists speak candidly about mental health, made with the same care as the music itself.

steps.label: Schools
steps.body: SoS High School gives students practical tools to explore emotions, identity, coping, and connection through the music they already listen to.

steps.label: Community
steps.body: Mental-health conversations and resources at concerts, festivals, and campuses, where young people already connect through music.

groups.label: Artists
groups.heading: Artist storytelling
groups.intro: Artists can be uniquely powerful trusted messengers. Their stories normalize difficult experiences, reduce stigma, model coping and help-seeking, and remind someone struggling that they are not alone. We don't ask artists to deliver mental-health messages; we make creative work with them that they are proud to share.

cards.title: Song That Found Me at the Right Time
cards.what: A film series where an artist covers the song that helped them through a difficult time and talks about what else helped: therapy, meditation, movement, community.
cards.who: Young people who find it easier to hear a hard truth from an artist they trust than from a pamphlet.
cards.happens: We record an intimate cover and conversation with each artist and publish it across YouTube and social. The series is produced in partnership with the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline and Vibrant Emotional Health. It draws on the Papageno effect: hearing real stories of getting through a crisis can spark hope and encourage help-seeking.
cards.proof: Featured in Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, AfroPunk, and MTV. Artists include Sharon Van Etten, Meshell Ndegeocello, Bartees Strange, SASAMI, CHAI, Geese, and Skullcrusher.

cards.title: Social Impact Media
cards.what: Personal, intimate films, photography, and social content built with artists and partners to reach fan bases through relatable stories and a shared connection to music.
cards.who: Artists, labels, festivals, and mission-aligned organizations who want mental-health content that does not feel like a PSA.
cards.happens: Long-form films (5 to 7 minutes), cross-platform social cuts, short PSAs (30 to 90 seconds), and live activations, often tied to Mental Health Awareness Month, Suicide Prevention Month, and World Mental Health Day.
cards.proof: Built on the same storytelling craft as the 988 series.

groups.label: Schools
groups.heading: SoS High School
groups.intro: We're not telling teenagers to listen to music. That would be absurd. We take advantage of the fact that they already do, and turn it into tools they can keep using long after the program ends.

cards.title: SoS HS
cards.what: A structured, music-driven mental wellness program for high schools, rooted in Social and Emotional Learning. It is not therapy and not crisis response. It builds emotional literacy and connection through an entry point students already trust.
cards.who: School counselors, SEL leads, advisory and health educators, and any school that needs a preventative approach it can run now.
cards.happens: Across five sessions students learn how music affects the brain and nervous system, build playlists tied to emotional states, explore how lyrics shape identity, take part in listening labs that spark peer dialogue, and reflect through guided journaling and discussion. Facilitated by school staff or SoS personnel, with minimal prep and no extra staffing.
cards.proof: Grew out of 2023 programs in two NYC public high schools, funded by MTV's Mental Health Action Day. Now piloting in Washington, DC, and being evaluated with NYU's Ripollés Lab. Partners include 988, Save The Music Foundation, Loveland Foundation, TikTok, SoundCloud, and the U.S. Department of Education.

cta.label: Bring SoS HS to your school

cards.title: Artist Visit
cards.what: A single high-impact event where an artist performs, then co-facilitates small groups with a therapist about coping, identity, and connection.
cards.who: Schools that want one event rather than the full program, or a way to start.
cards.happens: An artist-led session built around a mental-health theme, with a clear handoff to local care. This is the format that proved the idea in 2023: students who had turned down every other kind of support opened up.
cards.proof: Past artists include Erick the Architect, Pink Siifu, Cleo Reed, Bryndon Cook, deem spencer, and Maassai.

groups.label: Community
groups.heading: Music and community
groups.intro: Rather than waiting for someone to seek out a mental-health organization, we bring resources, conversations, and opportunities for connection into the spaces people already trust: concerts, festivals, campuses, and cultural events.

cards.title: The Song That Found Me table
cards.what: Instead of handing out pamphlets, we invite people to write down the song that found them at the right time and the story behind it. People tell us about grief, anxiety, friendship, breakups, and identity, all through music.
cards.who: Fans at tour stops and festivals, especially in places where local care is hard to find.
cards.happens: We partner with a local mental-health professional and a member of the 988 Lifeline, who demystify getting help. We hand out wallet crisis cards with a QR code to affordable, culturally informed local and national resources, and collect the cards and stories.
cards.proof: Tours and festivals joined include 6LACK's Since I Have a Lover, Courtney Barnett's Here and There, Re:SET, The National's Homecoming, Newport Folk, Governors Ball, and Hinterland.

cards.title: Listening parties, panels, and Feedback Sessions
cards.what: Events where music meets a guided conversation about a mental-health theme, from intimate listening parties to our Feedback Sessions with musicians, writers, and clinicians.
cards.who: Music fans, students, and the artists, writers, and mental-health professionals who take part.
cards.happens: Past themes include getting un-stuck, gender identity, working through childhood trauma, and coping with depression and anxiety. Sessions stay conversational, moving from naming a problem to ways of coping with it. On campuses we run the same format with student groups and wellness staff.
cards.proof: Produced with partners including OFFAIR, Republic Records, National Sawdust, UCLA's Semel Institute, and Columbia School of the Arts.
